Four unrelated topics so the RERANK_TOP_K=8 grounding set is selective rather than 'most of the corpus'. Reference-based metrics (Ctx Precision/Recall) are scored on the 'answerable' band only — an ideal answer that says 'the documents do not state this' gives Contextual Recall nothing to measure.

passages.text: Every production release requires two independent approvals: one from the owning team's tech lead and one from the release manager on duty. Approvals are recorded in the release ticket and the same person may not grant both.
An approval request that receives no response expires after 30 days. Expired requests must be raised again from scratch; there is no mechanism to extend one.
A release freeze applies during the last two weeks of December and the last three business days of each quarter. Only emergency releases proceed during a freeze.
Emergency releases may be deployed without prior approval, but require a VP sign-off recorded within 24 hours of the deploy.
Any release may be rolled back by the on-call engineer without seeking approval. A rollback is never treated as an incident in itself.
Release notes must be published before the deploy begins, not after it completes.
Every production release runs as a canary at 5 percent of traffic for a minimum of 30 minutes before wider rollout.
Database migrations must remain backward compatible with the previous release, so that a rollback does not require a schema change.
Feature flags default to off and must be removed from the codebase within 90 days of a full rollout.
Routine releases are permitted Tuesday to Thursday between 10:00 and 16:00 local time of the owning team.
No release may proceed while a Sev1 or Sev2 incident is active, including releases unrelated to the incident.
The release manager rota is published quarterly and covers one manager per business day.
Build artifacts must be signed. The deploy pipeline rejects an unsigned artifact and the rejection cannot be overridden.
A release blocked by failing tests cannot be overridden by any approver. The tests must pass or the change must be withdrawn.
The owning team must complete post-release verification within one hour of the deploy finishing.
Sev1 incidents must be acknowledged within 15 minutes, Sev2 within 2 hours, and Sev3 by the next business day.
A Sev1 is a complete outage or any loss of customer data affecting all customers of a service.
A Sev2 is a degraded service, or a major feature unavailable, where customers can still complete their primary task.
A Sev3 is a minor defect for which a documented workaround exists.
The on-call rota rotates weekly at 09:00 on Monday.
The outgoing engineer owns any incident opened before the handover, through to its resolution, even after the rota has moved on.
An incident commander is appointed for every Sev1 and is not the same person as the engineer performing the fix.
The public status page is updated within 30 minutes of a Sev1 being declared, and at least hourly until the incident is resolved.
A written postmortem is required for every Sev1 and Sev2, published within five business days of resolution.
Postmortems are blameless. No individual is named as a cause, and remediation items are owned by teams rather than people.
Customer communications are drafted by the support lead and approved by the incident commander before publication.
If a Sev1 page is not acknowledged within 15 minutes, the secondary on-call is paged automatically.
A secondary on-call is staffed for Sev1 escalation only; Sev2 and Sev3 have no secondary.
An incident channel is created automatically on declaration and archived once the postmortem is published.
A voice bridge is opened for every Sev1 and remains open until the incident is downgraded or resolved.
Audit records are retained for seven years and may not be deleted before that period elapses.
Application logs are retained for 90 days and are purged automatically. There is no manual purge path.
Customer data is deleted within 30 days of account closure, except where a legal hold applies.
Backups are retained for 35 days on a rolling basis and are encrypted with a separate key from the primary store.
A data access request is answered within 30 days of receipt.
Personal data must never be written to application logs, including in error messages and stack traces.
Data belonging to EU customers is stored and processed in the EU region only.
Encryption at rest is mandatory for every data store, including caches and message queues.
Identity must be confirmed before a deletion request is acted on; an unverified request is refused rather than queued.
Anonymised analytics that cannot be re-identified are retained indefinitely.
Data exports are provided in JSON format.
A legal hold suspends all deletion for the affected records until the hold is lifted by the legal team.
Subprocessors are listed publicly, and customers receive 30 days notice before a new subprocessor is engaged.
Any exception to a retention period requires written approval from the data protection officer.
A retention audit is performed quarterly and its findings are reported to the security committee.
Expense claims above 500 units require a second approver from outside the claimant's own reporting line.
Claims must be submitted within 60 days of the expense being incurred. Later claims are refused.
The per diem allowance is 65 units for domestic travel and 95 units for international travel.
Flights under six hours are booked in economy. Premium economy is permitted for flights of six hours or more.
Domestic hotel spend is capped at 200 units per night excluding tax.
A receipt is required for any single item above 25 units.
Alcohol is not reimbursable, including when it appears on an otherwise valid meal receipt.
Mileage in a personal vehicle is reimbursed at 0.45 units per mile.
The corporate card is used for travel wherever it is accepted. Personal card spend is reimbursed in the following payroll run.
Conference and training fees require manager pre-approval before booking.
Client entertainment claims must record the names of those present and the business purpose.
Foreign currency is converted at the rate on the transaction date, not the submission date.
A rejected claim may be resubmitted once, with a written justification addressing the reason for rejection.
Team events are capped at 50 units per head and require a manager to be present.
Equipment purchases are not expenses and must go through procurement, whatever their value.

questions.question: How many approvals does a production release need, and who gives them?
questions.expected_output: Two independent approvals: one from the owning team's tech lead and one from the release manager on duty. The same person may not grant both.

questions.question: What happens to an approval request that nobody responds to?
questions.expected_output: It expires after 30 days and must be raised again from scratch. There is no way to extend it.

questions.question: Can we deploy a release while a Sev1 is ongoing?
questions.expected_output: No. No release may proceed while a Sev1 or Sev2 is active, even if it is unrelated to the incident.

questions.question: How long does a canary run before wider rollout?
questions.expected_output: At least 30 minutes at 5 percent of traffic.

questions.question: When must a feature flag be removed from the code?
questions.expected_output: Within 90 days of a full rollout. Flags default to off.

questions.question: What is the acknowledgement time for a Sev1?
questions.expected_output: 15 minutes. Sev2 is 2 hours and Sev3 is the next business day.

questions.question: What counts as a Sev1?
questions.expected_output: A complete outage, or any loss of customer data, affecting all customers of a service.

questions.question: Who owns an incident that was opened just before the on-call handover?
questions.expected_output: The outgoing engineer owns it through to resolution, even after the rota has moved on.

questions.question: How quickly must a postmortem be published, and for which incidents?
questions.expected_output: Within five business days of resolution, for every Sev1 and Sev2.

questions.question: What happens if nobody acknowledges a Sev1 page in time?
questions.expected_output: The secondary on-call is paged automatically after 15 minutes.

questions.question: How long are audit records kept?
questions.expected_output: Seven years, and they may not be deleted before that.

questions.question: Can I manually purge application logs?
questions.expected_output: No. Application logs are retained 90 days and purged automatically; there is no manual purge path.

questions.question: When is customer data deleted after an account is closed?
questions.expected_output: Within 30 days of closure, unless a legal hold applies.

questions.question: What stops data from being deleted on the normal schedule?
questions.expected_output: A legal hold, which suspends all deletion for the affected records until the legal team lifts it.

questions.question: When does an expense claim need a second approver?
questions.expected_output: Above 500 units, and the second approver must be outside the claimant's reporting line.

questions.question: What is the per diem for international travel?
questions.expected_output: 95 units per day. Domestic is 65 units.

questions.question: Do I need a receipt for a 30 unit lunch?
questions.expected_output: Yes. A receipt is required for any single item above 25 units.

questions.question: My expense claim was rejected. Can I submit it again?
questions.expected_output: Yes, once, with a written justification addressing the reason for rejection.

questions.question: What is the parental leave entitlement?
questions.expected_output: The documents provided do not state a parental leave entitlement.

questions.question: Which cloud provider hosts the production database?
questions.expected_output: The documents provided do not name a cloud provider.

questions.question: How many vacation days do employees get each year?
questions.expected_output: The documents provided do not state a vacation entitlement.

questions.question: How often must passwords be rotated?
questions.expected_output: The documents provided do not state a password rotation period.

questions.question: Who approves a salary increase?
questions.expected_output: The documents provided do not describe salary approvals.

questions.question: What service credit do customers receive for downtime?
questions.expected_output: The documents provided do not describe service credits for downtime.

questions.question: What is the resolution deadline for a Sev1?
questions.expected_output: The documents state acknowledgement times but do not give a resolution deadline for a Sev1.

questions.question: What is the hotel cap for international travel?
questions.expected_output: The documents give a domestic hotel cap of 200 units per night but do not state an international one.

questions.question: How long are backups of audit records retained?
questions.expected_output: The documents state that audit records are kept seven years and that backups are kept 35 days, but do not state a retention period for backups of audit records specifically.

questions.question: How many approvals does a documentation-only change need?
questions.expected_output: The documents describe approvals for production releases but say nothing about documentation-only changes.

questions.question: What is the mileage rate for a motorcycle?
questions.expected_output: The documents give a mileage rate for a personal vehicle but do not state a separate motorcycle rate.

questions.question: How quickly is the status page updated for a Sev2?
questions.expected_output: The documents give status page timings for a Sev1 only and do not state them for a Sev2.
